finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /mirror fetches an attacker-supplied URL whose only validation is a suffix check (endswith 'example.com'), which is bypassable with an attacker-owned domain such as evilexample.com resolving to internal or metadata addresses. Blind SSRF with a response-length oracle; MEDIUM.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 — url query parameter on GET /mirror (unauthenticated)

trace.note: url: str bound from query string
if not host.endswith('example.com'): raise 400 — suffix check, not strict set membership; evilexample.com passes
r = await c.get(url) fetches original unparsed url; no resolved-IP check; httpx does not follow redirects by default
return {'len': len(r.text)} — only response length returned (blind)
ALLOWED_SUFFIX='.example.com' defined but unused; check hardcodes 'example.com' without dot boundary

finding.guards_checked: Suffix check at mirror.py:13 (bypassable, does not close per ssrf/SKILL.md); no scheme restriction (httpx limits to http/https, not exploitable); no resolved-IP/RFC-1918/link-local/metadata block (absent); no DNS rebinding pin (absent); redirects not followed by default in httpx>=0.20 (no redirect risk, unverified version — no lockfile); no authentication on route (absent); /ping at mirror.py:20-24 uses hardcoded URL (not a finding).
